items.headline: SpaceX is seeking roughly $40 billion in debt — about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade bonds — to buy Nvidia AI chips, in a deal expected to close in 2027
items.why: Financing chip purchases with investment-grade debt rather than cash treats compute capacity itself as collateral, raising the stakes for lenders if AI-driven revenue growth ever disappoints.

items.headline: AI cloud provider Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion valuation after its contracted backlog surged from about $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September, driven largely by a roughly $35 billion commitment from Anthropic
items.why: A backlog tripling in three months on the back of one customer's commitment shows how concentrated AI-compute demand really is, and how exposed providers are if that single buyer's plans shift.

items.headline: Marvell set a long-term target of $70-90 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031, up from about $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026, and raised its fiscal 2028 target to roughly $20 billion
items.why: Guidance implying a nearly tenfold revenue jump in five years only holds together if AI infrastructure spending keeps compounding at today's pace, making it a useful gauge of how much extrapolation is baked into chip-supply-chain valuations.

items.headline: Nvidia's market value approached $6 trillion after the company authorized a $150 billion share buyback, while Constellation Energy jumped 14.8% on a 20-year nuclear power deal to supply Google's AI data centers
items.why: A buyback that large signals Nvidia sees no better use for its own cash than its own stock, and a two-decade power contract for a single AI buildout shows how far down the supply chain the AI trade now reaches.

items.why: Crypto selling off in lockstep with a Middle East oil shock rather than on crypto-specific news confirms it is still trading as a leveraged risk-sentiment asset, not an independent safe haven.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs swung back to net inflows in early October, taking in $134.4 million over October 1-2 — led by BlackRock's IBIT with nearly $200 million on October 1 — after a $148.7 million outflow on September 30
items.why: A flow reversal this quick shows institutional demand for bitcoin exposure is still shallow enough to turn on a single weak print, not yet a steady structural bid.

items.headline: The CFTC issued guidance letting exchanges strip expiration dates from certain securities-index perpetual futures through October 20, and its chairman outlined draft rules on customer-asset segregation while naming bitcoin and ether as commodities, as Binance rolled out an AI trading-agent platform already handling over 280,000 daily calls
items.why: Perpetual-style products and a commodities designation moving from talk to actual guidance is the regulatory groundwork that has to be in place before US-regulated venues can offer crypto derivatives at the scale traditional futures markets already do.

items.headline: The US trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion in August, above the $102.0 billion estimate and July's revised $92.8 billion, with the import increase linked partly to industrial supplies and capital goods tied to AI-infrastructure buildout
items.why: A deficit growing because the US is importing the physical inputs for its own AI boom means that buildout is starting to show up as a drag on the trade balance, not just as a stock-market story.

items.headline: G7 nations moved to release 100 million barrels of strategic oil reserves over four months, helping pull WTI and Brent off their highs on October 6
items.why: A coordinated reserve release is a tool governments reach for when they want to cap a price before it becomes a political or inflation problem, so the move itself signals how seriously the Hormuz risk premium is being taken in Washington and other capitals.

items.headline: Iran's IRGC targeted at least seven oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz over five days, including two Kuwaiti vessels and three UAE-linked ships, with two reportedly set on fire
items.why: An attack rate this sustained against vessels from multiple flag states, not just those tied to the US or Israel, raises the odds that the risk eventually hits a tanker whose home country has no stake in staying out of the conflict.

items.headline: The 30-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5.7% on October 5 — its highest in 24 years — before easing to about 5.65%, as markets priced roughly a 70-85% chance of one more Fed rate hike by year-end and the dollar index pushed back above 102
items.why: A 24-year high on the long bond means the market is pricing a genuinely different rate regime, not just a pause, which raises the financing cost of everything from mortgages to the AI-infrastructure debt deals making headlines this week.
